html:
Oleg, called the Wise or the Seer, was a Varangian (Viking) prince who, by the Primary Chronicle, ruled the Rus' from about 879 to 912 and made Kyiv their capital. Almost all we know comes from that chronicle, written two centuries later, and some of it is legend; his birth date is unknown.

The chronicle says he was a kinsman of Rurik, the Varangian ruler of Novgorod, and ruled for Rurik's young son Igor. In 882 he went south down the Dnieper, killed Kyiv's rulers Askold and Dir, who are said to have led the Rus' attack on Constantinople of 860, and took the city. That joined the two ends of the river road from the Baltic to the Black Sea, and is taken as the founding of Kyivan Rus'. He made the Polans, the Severians and other Slav tribes pay tribute to Kyiv instead of the Khazars.

In 907, the chronicle says, his fleet came to Constantinople, put on wheels to sail over land, and he nailed his shield to the city gate. The treaty of 907 and a second in 911 gave Rus' merchants rights in the city. Legend says a seer foretold that his horse would kill him; years after the horse died, a snake crawled from its skull and bit him.
